newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Labour tops NZ poll for first time since 1993.
newsitem.headline: Labour tops NZ poll for first time since 1993.

text.p: New Zealand's Labour Party has topped a monthly national TV One's political opinion poll for the first time since 1993, the station reported on Monday.
Labour's support rose six points to 42 from last month.
The governing National Party fell three points to 39 percent while its coalition partner, New Zealand First, fell one to five percent.
The left-wing Alliance Party fell two points to six percent, free market Act down one to five.
Translated into seats, Labour would have 52, National 48, the Alliance eight and NZ First and Act six each.
Labour leader Helen Clark was the preferred prime minister with 21 percent support followed by Prime Minister Jim Bolger on 20, down three points.
SOE Minister Jenny Shipley, recently tipped as a possible successor to Bolger, rose 3.6 percent to six percent in the preferred prime minister stakes.
Disapproval of the centre-right coalition government's performance rose five points to 75 percent.
